answer: A practical defence is Telescope time allocation with observatory records. It rests on telescope nights allocated by an observatory, which gives every honest agent a pearl that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that telescope nights allocated by an observatory — so privacy survives, and the kernel is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. The defence holds because the cost is per identity and the reward is per identity too — the umber cancels out, and the farm is left with nothing but the bill.
